question: Under the National Immunisation Programme in India, a primigravida with unknown previous tetanus immunisation status presents at 16 weeks. What is the correct Td vaccination schedule?

answers.text: Single dose of Td at booking, no further doses needed.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A single dose is insufficient for a woman with no prior immunisation. The schedule requires two doses separated by at least 4 weeks.

answers.text: Two doses of Td — first dose as early as possible, second dose at least 4 weeks later (and at least 2 weeks before expected delivery).

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. For a primigravida with unknown or no prior tetanus immunisation, two doses of Td are given: first at booking (earliest possible), second ≥4 weeks later and ≥2 weeks before EDD.

answers.text: Three doses of Td given at 16, 20, and 28 weeks.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Three doses are not part of the routine pregnancy Td schedule. Two doses suffice for primary immunisation during pregnancy for an unimmunised woman.

answers.text: Td is contraindicated in the first trimester and should be deferred to after 20 weeks.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Td (tetanus-diphtheria) is safe in all trimesters. There is no restriction to after 20 weeks — early initiation ensures both doses are completed before delivery.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the NIP schedule: unimmunised primigravida needs 2 Td doses ≥4 weeks apart, both completed ≥2 weeks before expected delivery.
Correct. Two Td doses, ≥4 weeks apart, earliest possible start — both completed ≥2 weeks before EDD.
